solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A thousand small homes over island capital

indicators.note: in an across clue, turning something over flips its order so it reads from right to left

blocks.note: K is the standard abbreviation for a thousand
cots are small cottages
a holm is a small island, often in a river

explanation.surface: A property survey of a thousand little cottages overlooking an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reverses everything before it, the thousand included, not just the homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockholm is the seat of government of Sweden, its chief city and administrative centre.

clue.text: Son to pay for work space for loads

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written
a wage is what an employee is paid for work

explanation.surface: A son having to pay for a workspace to store his loads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For work' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition: a wage is pay for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowage is the room available on a ship or vehicle for packing cargo away.

clue.text: Have a debt to those in power

indicators.note: the letters sitting inside a word are the ones taken, not the whole word

blocks.note: the middle three letters of this word

explanation.surface: Being indebted to the people who rule over you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those in power' reads as the rulers, but here it means the letters in the word power.
explanation.definitionFit: To be obliged to repay someone money is exactly what it means to be indebted to them.

clue.text: Zany skier after one’s gone missing visits ski resort

indicators.note: something that has gone is no longer there, so a letter is dropped
zany means wildly eccentric, so the remaining letters are scrambled
a visitor goes inside someone's place, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: taken as written before losing a letter
one is the Roman numeral I
something missing is lost

explanation.surface: A crazy skier, after a friend has disappeared, turns up at a ski resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's gone' reads as a person leaving, but it means the numeral one leaves the skier. Klosters is a Swiss ski resort favoured by the British royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Klosters is a well-known winter sports village in the Swiss canton of Graubünden.

clue.text: Peaceful havens nomad seeks regularly

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A desert nomad often goes looking for peaceful refuges.
explanation.walkthrough: Start from the second letter and take every other one across both words.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is used figuratively for any calm refuge from surrounding stress or bustle.

clue.text: Insane to anger Number One close to Spanish government?

blocks.note: insane means mad
to rile someone is to anger them
No. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A crazy plot to enrage the Prime Minister, who is close to the Spanish government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number One' looks like a single phrase for a leader, but it splits: Number gives the letters and One starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrileño lives in Madrid, the Spanish capital and seat of its government, so is physically near it.

clue.text: Very light, perhaps, the cost of travelling around Lima

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a fare is the price of a journey
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Travelling round Lima, Peru, is very cheap, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very light' reads as 'extremely light', but a Very light is a signal flare fired from a Very pistol, named after its inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Very light is one particular kind of coloured signal flare, hence 'perhaps' marking an example.

clue.text: Run round tree, creating quite an impression

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: to fly is to run away or flee
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Someone running rings round a tree makes quite a spectacle of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly in the sense of flee is how 'run' gives FLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flashy is showy and ostentatious, designed to attract attention and dazzle onlookers.

clue.text: A … do … mi/E … la one plays in this style

definitions.text: A … do … mi/E … la one plays in this style

indicators.note: to play with something is to move it about, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the note names and letters taken as written, ellipses ignored

explanation.surface: A fragment of sol-fa notation followed by the remark that one plays in this musical style.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the letters and the description: the Aeolian mode runs from A to A, that is from la to la, so the music notes fit the style.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aeolian mode is the medieval church scale matching the natural minor, played on the white keys from A.

clue.text: Kill off melon plant growing from within

blocks.note: to end something is to finish it off
the ogen is a small sweet variety of melon

explanation.surface: Killing a melon plant that is growing from the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Melon plant' looks like one item, but the melon ends the wordplay and 'plant' begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An endogen is an old botanical term for a monocotyledon, whose stem was thought to thicken by internal additions.

clue.text: Oppressive old emperor no longer working

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Nero was a Roman emperor
US is short for unserviceable, meaning useless

explanation.surface: A tyrannical former emperor who has now retired.
explanation.walkthrough: US, for unserviceable, is a crossword staple for something broken or no longer working.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous burden weighs heavily on someone, just as an oppressive one does.

clue.text: Worked on encasing Egyptian god in precious stone

indicators.note: to encase is to enclose completely, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: to do a room is to work on it
Amon, or Amun, was the chief god of Thebes

explanation.surface: A craftsman working on setting an Egyptian idol within a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked on' sounds like part of a jewellery scene, but it is a single verb giving DID.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is the hardest and most valuable gemstone, the classic example of a jewel.

clue.text: A smart cravat or tie, primarily

definitions.text: A smart cravat or tie, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letters are taken

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Describing a smart neckpiece: a cravat or tie, primarily.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both supplies the letters and describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad neckband worn looped under the chin, a formal kind of cravat.

clue.text: Ruin chinchilla, perhaps when adjusting her top

indicators.note: adjusting something means moving it into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the chinchilla is a breed of long-haired cat, so 'perhaps' marks an example
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spoils her chinchilla while straightening her top.
explanation.walkthrough: The chinchilla wants to be the rodent, but it is also a cat breed, which is what the wordplay needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a disaster that brings total ruin, so the two nouns are close synonyms.

clue.text: Cutting illumination on front of stage

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of this word
lighting is illumination

explanation.surface: Reducing the lights at the front of a theatre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' puts the lighting after the S. 'Cutting' is not reducing but hurtful, as in a cutting remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A slighting comment is disparaging and hurtful, just like a cutting one.

clue.text: Berne et al. curiously open to incomers

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the letters are strangely ordered

blocks.note: taken as written, the full stop ignored

explanation.surface: Swiss cities like Berne are oddly welcoming to newcomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Berne et al.' looks like a list of Swiss cities, but its nine letters, ignoring the stop, are the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere you are able to go into is accessible and welcoming for people arriving.

clue.text: Ask for God’s protection for guarding weak and innocent

indicators.note: to guard something is to keep it surrounded and protected

blocks.note: to bless someone is to ask God to protect them
a lame excuse is a weak one

explanation.surface: A prayer for divine protection over the weak and the innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: The long first phrase is all one piece of wordplay, and 'guarding' tells it to wrap round the weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone blameless has done nothing wrong and deserves no fault, so they are guiltless.

clue.text: Soon girl must get round in

indicators.note: a thing placed in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: Ann is a girl's name
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A girl will soon have to get a round of drinks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a round in' is pub talk for buying drinks; here the round is simply the letter O, placed in the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word meaning shortly or in a little while.

clue.text: Facing work sitting for artist

blocks.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
a model posing is sitting for a painter

explanation.surface: A model is facing a job sitting for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: OP for opus is a standard crossword abbreviation for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Things on opposing sides are placed opposite each other, facing one another directly.

clue.text: Endure explosion — not the first in blitz

indicators.note: the first in a word is its opening letter
not means without, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: a blast is an explosion
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Holding out through a bombing raid in the Blitz, the German bombing of London in 1940-41.
explanation.walkthrough: The explosion loses the first letter of blitz.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or hold out through difficulty, which is what enduring means.

clue.text: Sucker punch victim

blocks.note: to lam is to hit or thrash
prey is a victim of a predator

explanation.surface: The target of a sucker punch, an unexpected blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker punch' reads as one phrase, but 'Sucker' alone is the definition: the lamprey has a round sucking mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamprey is an eel-like fish that clamps onto its host with a disc-shaped sucking mouth.

clue.text: Butterfly in Australia of no recognisable type

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: AUS is the abbreviation for Australia
the morpho is a large tropical butterfly

explanation.surface: A butterfly found in Australia that fits no known classification.
explanation.walkthrough: The morpho is the iridescent blue butterfly of Central and South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorphous means shapeless, lacking any definite form or structure that could be classified.

clue.text: Reticent about skin growth that’s looking dark

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: a reticent person is shy
a wart is a small growth on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone who is shy about a mole that is darkening.
explanation.walkthrough: The shy piece splits after its first letter to hold the wart.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarthy complexion is dusky or dark-skinned in appearance.

clue.text: Taken off course I’m upended by slide on ice

indicators.note: upended means turned upside down, which in a down clue flips the letter order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a sled slides over snow and ice

explanation.surface: A tobogganer admits being thrown off course, tipped over by a sled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slide on ice' is a noun phrase here: a sledge, not the act of skidding.
explanation.definitionFit: To be misled is to be led the wrong way, literally or figuratively deceived.

clue.text: Slight inebriation — nearly going wrong in confusion

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
one thing in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: a mess is a state of confusion
to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: Being a little drunk is almost leading one astray in bewilderment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry' is British understatement for mildly drunk, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To be merry, in British usage, is to be pleasantly tipsy from drink.

clue.text: Drain small jug

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: An instruction to empty a little jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drain' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, the channel that carries waste water.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewer is an underground pipe carrying away waste water, a kind of large drain.

clue.text: Piece of Amilcare Ponchielli’s making a comeback?

indicators.note: a piece of something is a part of it, so the letters come from inside
coming back means travelling the opposite way, so the order is turned round

blocks.note: the last three letters of the first name and first two of the surname

explanation.surface: Is a work by the Italian composer Ponchielli being revived?
explanation.walkthrough: Ponchielli is best known for his opera La Gioconda, so the letters read backwards also describe one of his pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ponchielli was a nineteenth-century Italian composer whose chief works were stage dramas set to music.

clue.text: Drive back concerned with vibration

blocks.note: re means regarding or concerning
a pulse is a regular throb or vibration

explanation.surface: A worry about the shaking while driving in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive back' reads like reversing a car; here it means to force back an attacker.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attack is to repel it, forcing the enemy to retreat.

clue.text: Punish favourite dog

blocks.note: to whip someone is to punish them
a teacher's pet is their favourite

explanation.surface: Disciplining a favourite dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a single scene, but the two verbs split cleanly into two words that join end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: The whippet is a slim, fast greyhound-like breed used for racing.

clue.text: An irrational terror’s beginning in bed?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: pi is an irrational number, one that cannot be written as a fraction
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Is a phobia, an irrational fear, starting while lying in bed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational terror' pretends to be a phobia; the irrational is a number. 'Pit' is British slang for bed, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British speech one's pit is one's bed, as in getting out of your pit.

clue.text: Unknown deli junked produce

indicators.note: junked means thrown out as rubbish, so the letters land in disorder

blocks.note: in algebra an unknown quantity is x, y or z
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mystery delicatessen threw its fresh food away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' looks like fruit and vegetables, but the definition is the noun meaning output.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm's yield is its output of crops, the amount it produces.

clue.text: Active agent embracing both sides

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: a secret agent is a spy
right written in full plus L for left

explanation.surface: A double agent playing for both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The two sides are right and left, one spelt out and one abbreviated to L.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprightly person is lively and energetic, full of spirit despite perhaps their age.
